subject: economics
title: Shifts, Surpluses & Shocks
welcome_lead: A frost wipes out the strawberry crop. A celebrity sips matcha and demand soars. Calculate what happens to price and quantity.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics calculations adventure: demand and supply shifts, surpluses, shortages and equilibrium maths.
final_note: Markets dance to the tune of countless shocks. Now try the exam-style stretch!

concepts.def: Entire curve moves left or right.
Change along a curve due to own-price change.
A good used in place of another.
A good used together with another.

walkthroughs.body_html: Suppose a viral TikTok promotes oat milk. At every price, more people now want it. The entire demand curve shifts rightward. New equilibrium: higher price AND higher quantity. Other rightward shifters: rising incomes (normal goods), pricier substitutes, cheaper complements.

walkthroughs.h2: How a frost shifts supply left
walkthroughs.body_html: Bad weather destroys 30% of the strawberry crop. At every price, less is available. Supply curve shifts leftward. New equilibrium: higher price, lower quantity. Other leftward supply shifters: higher input costs, new taxes, tighter regulation.

Original: Qd = 80 - P, Qs = 20 + P, so equilibrium P=30, Q=50. Suppose demand rises by 20 at every price: new Qd = 100 - P. Set 100 - P = 20 + P → 80 = 2P → P = 40, Q = 60. Price rose £10; quantity rose 10 units.

mcqs.q: Petrol and cars are complements. If petrol prices double, what happens to demand for cars?
options: Demand curve shifts right
Demand curve shifts left
Movement up the demand curve
Supply curve shifts left

mcqs.q: When price is ABOVE equilibrium, what occurs?
options: A shortage forms
A surplus forms and price falls
Demand shifts right
Supply shifts left

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A change in price shifts the demand curve.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
Demand always falls when supply increases.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
Inflation is when prices are high.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A sustained rise in the general price level over time — reducing the purchasing power of money. Measured by the percentage change in a price index.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Surplus”?
options: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
A good used in place of another.
A good used together with another.
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Shortage”?
options: Entire curve moves left or right.
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Change along a curve due to own-price change.
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Movement”?
options: Change along a curve due to own-price change.
A good used together with another.
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Substitute”?
options: A good used in place of another.
A good used together with another.
Change along a curve due to own-price change.
Entire curve moves left or right.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Complement”?
options: Entire curve moves left or right.
Change along a curve due to own-price change.
A good used together with another.
A good used in place of another.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Shift”?
options: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Change along a curve due to own-price change.
A good used in place of another.
Entire curve moves left or right.
